definition: Interest on finance lease liabilities, as the lease note discloses it.
note: Backlog #497: added to interest in the cost of debt (D8) when the average debt counted finance_lease_liabilities at its year ends. WMT only: Walmart's interest line (InterestExpenseDebt) is debt only. Its income-statement 'Finance lease' line (wmt:FinanceLeaseAndFinancingObligationInterestExpense, 481M FY2026) also holds interest on financing obligations Warren does not count as debt; this tag is the lease note's 'Interest on lease obligations' (383M FY2026), whose liability is the FinanceLeaseLiability counted. MSFT (backlog #527): Microsoft's interest total already includes it (10-K Item 7), so it is never added to that total; it is summed with interest_paid_on_debt, which replaces the total in Microsoft's cost of debt.

definition: Cash paid for interest on debt, before any interest is capitalised.
note: Backlog #527: Microsoft's debt note, "cash paid for interest on our debt" (rounded to $0.1 billion from FY2016). Its interest expense is net of the interest it capitalises (10-K Item 7, FY2025 and FY2026: "higher capitalization of debt interest expense") and it tags no capitalised amount, so its cost of debt (D8) reads this plus finance_lease_interest in place of the expense when the average debt counted finance_lease_liabilities at both year ends and no short-term borrowings or commercial paper at either (the paper's interest is paid as a discount, not in this figure). MSFT only: other companies' InterestPaid can include lease interest or be net of capitalised interest.

definition: Interest capitalised during the period, as the cash-flow statement discloses it.
note: Backlog #533: ExxonMobil's interest expense is net of the interest it capitalises into projects (ASC 835-20; 1,534M against 603M expensed in FY2025), so its cost of debt (D8) adds this to the expense: interest incurred, on the basis of its debt, which already holds its finance leases. Tagged from the FY2019 10-K on (FY2017 first in 0000034088-20-000016); equal to InterestCostsCapitalized where both are filed (FY2017 to FY2020). XOM only at first; JNJ added by backlog #540 (its income statement's "Interest expense, net of portion capitalized"; J&J files the amount as InterestCostsCapitalized only, so this row is for a future cash-flow figure, the same amount by meaning). Another company's capitalised figure must be checked against its interest line and debt first.

definition: Interest capitalised during the period, as the cash-flow statement discloses it.
note: Backlog #533: ExxonMobil's interest capitalised in the 10-Ks to FY2020, the same figure as InterestPaidCapitalized where both are filed. Backlog #540: J&J's interest capitalised into the construction of facilities and equipment (property note: 49M, 63M and 70M in FY2021, FY2020 and FY2019, 0000200406-22-000022), every year; its interest expense line is net of it and it counts no finance-lease liability or interest, so expense + capitalised is interest incurred on the debt Warren divides by. JNJ and XOM only.

definition: Interest expense that is not on debt, as the filing discloses it.
note: Backlog #533 (analyst): ExxonMobil's interest expense includes non-debt-related interest (segment note, Corporate and Financing: 300M in 2025, 400M in 2024, 200M in 2023 in 0000034088-26-000045; FY2023 and FY2024 restated from 234M and 437M), so its cost of debt (D8) takes it out of the expense before adding interest_capitalized. Left out when below zero (FY2013: -123M) or not below the expense. XOM only.

definition: Gain or loss on extinguishing debt before maturity (a gain is positive), as the filing discloses it.
note: Backlog #610: Coca-Cola records the gain or loss on paying debt off early in its interest expense line (every 10-K's text, 2013 to 2024: charges of 459M in FY2020 and 559M in FY2021 in 0000021344-22-000009, Note 10), so its cost of debt (D8) takes it out of the interest. Two 10-Ks put the year before's figure under their own year (misdated_facts.csv), which D8 leaves out. KO only: P&G books its FY2021 charge outside interest, and another company's figure must be checked against its interest line first.
